method: Visual inspection of actual native-final Unity player PNGs, checked against the final receipt and accepted transparent frame artwork.

checks.name: Caster-foot charge
checks.detail: East-flight capture shows the teal/gold charge around the caster feet while the approved character cast action runs.

checks.name: Directional travel
checks.detail: West and east flight captures show the core between caster and target; left travel has its tail on the right and right travel has its tail on the left.

checks.name: Telegraph and strike feet
checks.detail: All three actual target positions carry their own synchronized foot rings and purple strike instances; the strike tips remain within their image rectangles.

checks.name: Chest reaction and number layer
checks.detail: Single and three-target reaction captures show gold hit stars on the upper body, with one legible -100 number above each actual target and overhead bars still visible.

checks.name: Alpha and clipping
checks.detail: No opaque strip rectangles, magenta key color, missing sprite cells or visible frame-edge clipping in the inspected captures.

checks.name: Unique results and cleanup
checks.detail: Final receipt has one damage event per actual target, one shared damage frame, one number per target, and zero active FX after cleanup; aborted/skipped flight and telegraph cases have no late result.

scope: Offline production-presenter acceptance with synthetic 100 damage outcomes; no server settlement claim.
timingNotes: flight-mid is a phase label and is not an assertion of an exact 50 percent trajectory position.
At 6x and target 15fps the short hit pose can be skipped by frame quantization; visual reaction inspection uses the normal 1x captures.

GPU frame readback and initial resource loading still introduce some frame spikes. The first cold 1201-west case peaked at about 1.10 seconds per frame; warm normal cases first hit at about 1.16-1.17 seconds and 6x/15fps cases at about .33 seconds. These captures are not a frame-rate performance benchmark; the deterministic 15/30fps checks are in the passing specialized tests.
